Location: Indore, Madhya Pradesh
Work Mode: Work From Office
Experience: 0-1 year (freshers with strong fundamentals welcome)


About the Role




We're looking for a curious, sharp-thinking QA Engineer at the start of their career to join our Indore office. You don't need years of experience you need a mind that breaks things on purpose, asks "what if?" before anyone else does, and is genuinely excited about how AI is reshaping the way software is tested.

You'll work alongside developers, product managers, and senior QA engineers to make sure what we ship actually works not just on the happy path, but in the messy real world our customers live in.

This is an on-site role. We believe early-career engineers grow fastest sitting next to the people they learn from — whiteboarding a test strategy, pairing on a tricky defect, and picking up context that never makes it into a ticket.




What You'll Do



Understand requirements deeply and translate them into clear, thorough test scenarios and test cases
Execute functional, regression, integration, and exploratory testing across web and desktop applications
Find, isolate, and report defects with precise reproduction steps, logs, and evidence
Think beyond the ticket — identify edge cases, boundary conditions, and negative scenarios that others miss
Verify fixes and own the quality of your assigned areas through the release cycle
Write and maintain basic automation scripts under guidance, and grow into owning them
Use AI tools to accelerate test design, data generation, log analysis, and exploratory coverage
Participate in sprint ceremonies, share risk findings early, and communicate status clearly



What We're Looking For




Testing Fundamentals

Solid grasp of SDLC, STLC, and the bug lifecycle
Knows the difference between test scenarios, test cases, and test data — and can write all three
Understands functional, regression, smoke, sanity, integration, UAT, and exploratory testing
Familiar with test design techniques: equivalence partitioning, boundary value analysis, decision tables

Logical & Dynamic Thinking (this matters most)

Can reason from a symptom back to a probable root cause instead of just reporting "it doesn't work"
Thinks in systems — understands that a change in one module can break three others
Adapts test approach when requirements shift mid-sprint instead of waiting for perfect clarity
Asks the uncomfortable question in refinement that saves a production incident later

Coding Knowledge

Working knowledge of at least one language (Java, Python, JavaScript, or C#)
Comfortable with basic programming constructs: loops, conditions, functions, data structures
Can read application code well enough to understand what a change actually affects
Basic SQL — able to write SELECT queries with JOINs to validate data
Exposure to Selenium, Playwright, Cypress, or similar is a strong plus
Familiarity with Git, REST APIs, and Postman

AI Thought Process

Actively uses AI assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) in day-to-day work, not just casually
Understands how to prompt effectively — and, more importantly, how to validate AI output rather than trust it blindly
Sees AI as a force multiplier for test coverage, not a replacement for thinking
Curious about AI-assisted test generation, self-healing automation, and intelligent defect triage

Communication

Writes bug reports that a developer can act on without a single follow-up question
Explains technical risk in plain language to non-technical stakeholders
Speaks up in meetings — raises concerns early rather than after the release
Collaborative and direct, without being defensive about feedback

Attitude

Genuinely eager to learn — picks up new tools and domains fast and without hand-holding
Takes ownership of quality rather than treating QA as a checklist step
Comfortable with ambiguity and asking for help at the right time



Nice to Have

Internship or academic project involving test automation
Exposure to CI/CD tools (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Bitbucket Pipelines)
Knowledge of API testing and basic performance testing concepts
Familiarity with Jira, TestRail, Zephyr, or similar test management tools
ISTQB Foundation Level certification
A GitHub profile with real projects — even small ones



Education

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, IT, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.




How We Evaluate

Our interview process is designed to test how you think, not what you've memorized:

Logical reasoning round — puzzles and scenario-based problem solving
Testing round — given a feature, design the test approach and find the edge cases
Coding round — basic programming and SQL
AI & tooling discussion — how you actually use AI in your workflow
Culture and communication conversation



Why Join Us

Mentorship from senior QA engineers from day one
Real ownership of features, not just ticket execution
A team that actively invests in AI-driven quality engineering
A clear growth path into automation, performance, or SDET roles
Collaborative on-site culture in our Indore office

About Ampity Infotech

Ampity Infotech is a cloud and DevOps engineering firm that helps growing companies design, build, and operate production-grade software and infrastructure on AWS. We work directly with client engineering and leadership teams, and we build AI-powered capabilities into client products as a core part of our delivery, not as a side experiment.




Role Summary

As an AI Engineer on Ampity's delivery team, you will design, build, and ship AI-powered capabilities for client products. The work spans applied LLM/GenAI engineering (RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, prompt design, evaluation) and classical ML/data science (model training, fine-tuning, feature engineering, deployment) depending on what an engagement calls for. You will be accountable for how these systems perform in production, meaning accuracy, latency, cost, and reliability, not just for a working prototype.




What You'll Own

Design and build LLM/GenAI-powered features: RAG pipelines, agentic or tool-calling workflows, prompt design, and integration with model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, etc.).
Build, fine-tune, and evaluate ML models where a classical or statistical approach fits the problem better than an LLM, including data preprocessing and feature engineering.
Design and run evaluation frameworks (offline evals, golden datasets, human-in-the-loop review) to measure accuracy, hallucination rate, and regressions before and after changes.
Deploy and operate AI/ML systems in production on AWS (SageMaker, Bedrock, Lambda, or EKS), with monitoring for drift, latency, and cost.
Own data pipelines that feed models and retrieval systems: ingestion, chunking, embeddings, and vector store management.
Apply security and responsible-AI practices: data handling, PII protection, prompt-injection defenses, and guardrails for AI-facing product surfaces.
Communicate model behavior, limitations, and trade-offs clearly to client engineering teams and non-technical stakeholders.
Produce implementation notes and handover documentation so client teams can operate and extend what you build.
Use AI-assisted coding tools as part of your own workflow, with the judgment to verify their output before it reaches production.



Required Qualifications

2-4 years of hands-on experience building and shipping AI/ML systems to production, not just research notebooks or proofs of concept.
Practical experience with LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock) and at least one GenAI framework such as LangChain or LlamaIndex.
Solid Python skills, including experience with ML/data libraries (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, or TensorFlow).
Experience building or operating RAG pipelines and working with vector databases or embedding stores (Pinecone, pgvector, OpenSearch, or similar).
Understanding of model evaluation methodology: metrics, test sets, and how to detect regressions or hallucinations.
Working knowledge of cloud platforms (AWS preferred) for deploying and serving models.
Ability to explain model behavior, limitations, and trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.



Nice to Have

Experience fine-tuning open-source or foundation models (LoRA/PEFT, instruction tuning).
Experience with agentic frameworks (LangGraph, AutoGen, or custom tool-calling orchestration).
Familiarity with MLOps tooling (MLflow, SageMaker Pipelines, Weights & Biases).
Exposure to data engineering (Airflow, Spark, dbt) for building training or retrieval datasets.
Prior experience in a client-facing consulting or applied AI product environment.



What We Value

Ampity looks for AI engineers who ship systems that hold up in production, not just demos that work once. In practice, that means we weigh these traits heavily in this role:

AI fluency with scepticism you use AI and model outputs to move faster, and you know how to verify them before they reach production.
Production ownership — you understand incidents, cost, drift, and maintenance, not just initial delivery.
Trade-off reasoning — you compare a classical ML approach, an LLM, or a simpler rule-based system against the client's real constraints, rather than defaulting to the newest technique.
Clarity — you can explain a model's behavior and limitations, including its uncertainty, to a teammate and to a client.
Knowledge transfer — you make the team and the client stronger rather than accumulating private expertise.



How to Apply

Apply on – ta@ampityinfotech.com
